comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Regex matches characters not handled in the escape mapping.**

The regex `/['"\\\b\f\n\r\t]/g` matches backspace (`\b`), form feed (`\f`), and tab (`\t`), but the `codes` object doesn't include mappings for them. These characters will pass through unescaped due to the `|| char` fallback.

Either remove these characters from the regex if they don't need escaping, or add them to the mapping for consistency:


<details>
<summary>🔧 Proposed fix to add missing escape mappings</summary>

```diff
     const codes: Record<string, string> = {
       "'": "\\'",
       '"': '\\"',
       "\\": "\\\\",
+      "\b": "\\b",
+      "\f": "\\f",
       "\n": "\\n",
-      "\r": "\\r"
+      "\r": "\\r",
+      "\t": "\\t"
     };
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/core-server/utils/safeString.ts` around lines 6 - 14, The regex
in the replace call inside safeString.ts includes \b, \f and \t but the codes
mapping object (codes) lacks entries for backspace, form-feed and tab so those
characters are left unescaped; update the codes object used by the str.replace
callback (the codes constant in the replace handler) to include mappings for
"\b": "\\b", "\f": "\\f" and "\t": "\\t" (or alternatively remove those
sequences from the regex), ensuring the replace callback returns the proper
escaped sequences for all characters matched by the regex.
```

</details>

<!-- fingerprinting:phantom:poseidon:ocelot -->

comments.author: yannbf
copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body:
The regex pattern includes `\b`, `\f`, and `\t` characters, but the `codes` mapping doesn't include escape sequences for these characters. This means when these characters are matched, the function falls back to `return codes[char] || char`, which returns the original character unchanged, defeating the purpose of including them in the regex.

Either add the missing escape codes to the mapping:
```
"\b": "\\b",
"\f": "\\f",
"\t": "\\t"
```

Or remove `\b\f\t` from the regex pattern if escaping them is not needed.
```suggestion
      "\b": "\\b",
      "\f": "\\f",
      "\n": "\\n",
      "\r": "\\r",
      "\t": "\\t"
```

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body:
The approach of escaping special characters in file paths and export names is fundamentally flawed for this use case. The sanitization is being applied to `componentFilePath` and `componentExportName` before they're passed to `generateStoryFile`. However:

1. In `get-new-story-file.ts`, the code uses Node.js path manipulation functions (`basename`, `dirname`, `extname`) on the already-escaped path. This will break because escaped characters like `\\'` or `\\n` are not valid file path characters.

2. The escaped strings are used directly in template literals to construct import statements (e.g., `import Component from './${basenameWithoutExtension}'`), which would generate syntactically invalid code with double-escaped characters.

3. File paths should be valid filesystem paths, not escaped JavaScript strings. The real file system won't have files with names like `button\\'s.tsx`.

Instead of escaping the inputs at the channel layer, sanitization should be applied at the point where the strings are inserted into generated code templates, or use a different approach like parameterized templates or proper AST generation. This would maintain valid file paths while protecting against injection in the generated code.
